text:
alex: Heads-up — a couple customers on Private VPC are hitting capacity ceilings during morning spikes. They're seeing long queues and client timeouts. Any short, prescriptive guidance we can share for customer-side admission control + graceful degradation? cc @maria @sachin

maria: TL;DR: recommend a token-bucket limiter per-tenant+model + a tiny local queue + explicit fallback ordering (smaller model -> truncated response -> 429). Keep it simple so infra teams can implement quickly. :thumbsup:

maria: Suggested defaults to start with (customer-configurable):
- local_queue_max: 50 requests
- token_refill_per_sec: map to reserved GPU capacity, e.g., 10 rps per vGPU for medium models
- burst: 3 * token_refill_per_sec
- max_wait_ms: 250ms (after that return graceful degradation)

maria: Example Envoy rate-limit style (pseudocode):
```
rate_limit: 
  domain: "redwood_vpc"
  descriptors: 
    - key: "tenant_id:model"
      token_bucket: 
        fill_interval: 1000ms
        tokens_per_fill: <refill_based_on_reserved_gpu>
        max_tokens: <burst>
```

sachin: Additions: expose `redwood_pool_utilization` and `redwood_allocated_gpus` metrics to customers (Prom). Then you can drive adaptive refill: shrink token_refill if pool_utilization > 0.85 for >30s. That avoids cascading queue growth.

sachin: Also, prefer 429 + `Retry-After` for client-visible admission control. Use 503 for server-level failures where we want clients to backoff longer. Example header:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-Redwood-Reason: queue_capacity
```

julie: For private deploys where autoscaling isn't available, recommend a builtin degrade chain the customer can configure: [primary: redwood/rdxlarge] -> [fallback: redwood/rdxsmall-quantized] -> [final: short-summary mode]. Provide a 2xx lightweight response if fallback used and include `X-Redwood-Degrade: model=rdxsmall` so apps can surface UX differences.

julie: Circuit-breaker pattern we use internally: fail-open cooldowns with hysteresis. Pseudocode: 
```
if (error_rate > 0.2 && util > 0.9) open_circuit(60s)
else if (util < 0.6) close_circuit()
```

alex: This is great. Can we give customers concrete numbers for mapping tokens -> GPU capacity? They keep asking how many requests per second a reserved 4xA100 pool should allow.

maria: Rough rule of thumb (highly workload-dependent):
- large gen models (10k context): ~0.5-2 rps per GPU
- medium/chat models (2k context): ~5-12 rps per GPU
- embedding/light models: 50-200 rps per GPU
So for a 4-GPU reserved pool running mixed-medium models, start with token_refill ~= 4 * 8 = 32 rps and tune from there.

sachin: Recommend customers run a short load test during onboarding: ramp to 2x target QPS and capture p95/p99 latency and `redwood_pool_queue_depth`. If p95 spikes > 2x, lower token_refill or add fallback.

maria: Quick NGINX example for a simple local limiter (customer side):
```
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=rl:10m rate=30r/s;
server {
  location /predict {
    limit_req zone=rl burst=60 nodelay;
    proxy_pass http://local-proxy;
  }
}
```

julie: Note on metrics: tell customers to alert on `redwood_pool_utilization > 0.9` and `queue_depth > local_queue_max`. If they have Prometheus + Alertmanager, a sample alert: 
```
- alert: RedwoodHighUtilization
  expr: redwood_pool_utilization > 0.9 for 2m
  labels: {severity: page}
```

sachin: Also call out networking quirks in some VPC setups: bursty client TCP connections can exhaust ENIs/NAT throughput even before GPU gets saturated. Recommend clients use HTTP/2 or keep-alive connections and limit concurrent connections per host.

alex: Ops question — what response semantics do we prefer we recommend for streaming RPCs? 429 doesn't always map well there.

maria: For streaming: prefer a short server-side pre-check that rejects immediately with a small JSON error (grpc status 8/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or HTTP 429) before opening long-lived stream. If the stream is allowed, add `X-Redwood-Queue-Position` headers first as soft telemetry.

ops-bot: alert: customer-cluster-123 queued_requests > 200 (action: rate-limit applied at edge)

julie: Packaging note — add a one-page runbook we can hand to customers with: config snippets (Envoy, NGINX, Node/Go client libs), default numbers, testing checklist, and a section on fallback ordering. Keep it < 1 page.

alex: Perfect. I'll draft the 1-pager and attach to onboarding. Thanks y'all. :rocket:
